chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), or he said, 'One of our companions asked him,' about the man who testifies for his father, or the father testifies for his son, or the brother for his brother. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that when it is good; his testimony for his father, and the father for his son, and the brother for his brother, is accepted.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a father for his son or brother for his brother accepted in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the testimony of close male relatives is valid provided they are *kayyiran* (upright/trustworthy), a ruling that distinguishes Shia jurisprudence from some Sunni schools which often restrict or disqualify close kin to prevent bias. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith, with scholars like Hisham ibn Salim serving as key transmitters of these legal nuances. This ruling underscores the principle that personal relationship does not inherently invalidate testimony, but rather the individual's moral integrity (*'adalah*) is the determining factor.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Ammar Bin Marwan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>’, or said, ‘One of our companions asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who testifies for his father, or the father testifies for his son, or the brother for his brother. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that when it was good, it would be allowed, his testimony for his father, and of the father for his son, and of the brother for his brother’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan who has narrated the following: “

I or a certain persons of our people asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who testifies for his father or a father testifies for his son or for his brother. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful if it is for a good cause. His testimony is permissible for his father as is the case with a father’s testimony for his son or a brother’s testimony for his brother.’”
